text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.6% today, reaching $410.74, driven by a sharp spike in crude oil prices following Saudi Arabia's pipeline closure from a drone attack. U.S. oil broke past $105 a barrel (up from the $97.26 level in today's data), and global crude topped $109.51, tightening energy supplies and boosting refiner margins—the profit spread between what refiners pay for crude and what they earn selling gasoline and diesel. With U.S. refineries already running near capacity at 97.8%, higher crude prices typically improve refiner profitability when they can pass costs through to end users.

The broader context is an escalating regional conflict: Houthi militants struck Saudi infrastructure again this week, and Iran's foreign minister is heading to China for talks, keeping geopolitical risk elevated. Refinery stocks like Marathon have climbed 10% over two weeks as the Iran-related supply tensions push oil prices higher, a trend that benefits crude processors more than it hurts them.
